content:
Over the past year, we've been eagerly awaiting the next-generation iPad mini update, and the news seems to be just around the corner. Aaron Perris revealed last week that the new device will feature the A20 Pro chip and narrower screen bezels, and we already know it will adopt an OLED display with a waterproof design.

While these upgrades are already quite attractive, my biggest expectation for the next iPad mini is actually on the software side.

After watching the iPhone Duo, I'm truly impressed by Apple's multitasking capabilities. The iPad's multitasking experience has always felt quite messy to me, but the iPhone Duo appears elegant and fluid.

On such a small screen, traditional windowed operations have never really suited the iPad mini. Users probably wouldn't want to stack too many windows on it. So I hope Apple can borrow a practical feature from the iPhone Duo: split view combined with picture-in-picture.

What I mean is, this experience is really top-notch. Currently on the iPad mini, in portrait mode, the picture-in-picture window cannot occupy the full width of the screen; even when it can, it either blocks part of the app content, or you have to manually resize it through window controls.

Bringing split video and app screens to the iPad mini's display seems like a no-brainer to me—especially considering the iPhone Duo and iPad mini have similar aspect ratios. At least for me personally, if this feature existed, I'd use the iPad mini in portrait mode far more often.

  • Logitech MX Master 4 mouse (Mac version)
  • AirTag 2 4-pack (precision finding improved by 50%!)
  • Belkin iPhone MagSafe 3-in-1 charging stand
  • MOFT iPhone MagSafe magnetic stand wallet
